PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Self-awareness means knowing who you are and why you matter. In this sub-strand you will say your name, notice what makes you different from other people, and learn that God made you. You will read Genesis 1:27 and Psalm 139:13 and thank God for making you His special creation.

## Strand 1.0: Creation
Sub-strand 1.1: Self-awareness
Suggested lessons: 2

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 1.0 Creation, Sub-strand 1.1 Self-awareness
• Psalm 139:13-14; Genesis 1:27

PAGE 2: Learning outcomes

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) mention his or her name for identification and self- awareness
b) recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God
c) acknowledge God as the creator
d) appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation

## Key inquiry questions
1. Why are you a special creation?

PAGE 3: How we will learn

## Learning experiences
• say their names
• state what is unique about them
• recite and meditate on Psalms 139:13 about being fearfully and wonderfully made
• read Genesis 1:27 about being, ‘created in the image and likeness of God’
• sing a song related to their uniqueness

## Core competencies
• Self-efficacy: the skill of knowing self is exhibited as learners say their names for identification.

## Values
• Respect: learners portray positive regard for self and others.

## Links to other learning areas
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners sing, dance, draw and colour pictures of faces depicting various emotions.
• English: speaking skills are applied as learners recite Bible verses.

PAGE 4: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique

LESSON 1: MY NAME AND WHAT MAKES ME UNIQUE
==========================================

## What you will learn
• Say his or her name clearly for identification.
• State what is unique about himself or herself.
• Explain that being unique means God made each person one of a kind.

Curriculum outcomes: a) mention his or her name for identification and self- awareness; b) recognise his or her uniqueness as a creation of God

## Introduction
When the teacher calls the register, you answer to your own name. That name tells people who you are. Knowing your name, and knowing what is special about you, is the start of self-awareness.

PAGE 5: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Notes 1

## Notes

Your name is the first way people identify you. It may be the name your parents gave you at birth, and it may include a family name. When you say it clearly, others know who is speaking. Saying your name is not showing off. It is a simple way of knowing yourself.

PAGE 6: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — What unique means

### What unique means
Unique means one of a kind. No other learner in the class is exactly like you. You may share a classroom, a language or a favourite game, but God made differences that belong to you.

Things that can be unique about you:

- Your full name
- Your face, height, voice and smile
- What you enjoy and what you can do well
- The way you think, feel and treat other people

Two children can both like singing and still be different people. One may be quiet. Another may speak quickly. Both are valuable.

PAGE 7: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Psalm 139:13

### Psalm 139:13
Psalm 139:13 says that God formed you inside your mother. He put you together with care before anyone else saw you. Psalm 139:14 says, "I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made." Fearfully, in this verse, means with great care and wonder. Wonderfully means in an amazing way.

You do not need to copy another child's face, voice or marks in order to matter. You already matter because God made you. When you recite Psalm 139:13, pause and thank God for the way He made you.

PAGE 8: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Showing respect

### Showing respect
Listen when a classmate says his or her name and what is special about them. Do not laugh at a difference. Positive regard for yourself and for others is respect.

## Key words
• self-awareness — knowing who you are
• unique — one of a kind; not exactly like anyone else
• identification — showing who a person is

PAGE 9: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
Amina says, "I wish I looked exactly like my friend so that people would like me." What can you tell her from this lesson?

Working:
1. God formed each person with care.
2. Psalm 139:14 says we are fearfully and wonderfully made.
3. Amina's own name, face and gifts already make her special.

Answer: She does not need to copy her friend. God made her unique, and that is something to thank Him for.

PAGE 10: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Say your name and what is unique about you

## Activity: Say your name and what is unique about you
You will need: Exercise book, Bible

1. Stand in a circle. Each learner says his or her full name clearly.

2. Each learner states one thing that is unique about himself or herself.

3. The class listens without laughing and thanks each speaker.

4. Together, recite Psalm 139:13 and sit quietly for a short time to think about being wonderfully made.

5. Sing a short song about being special to God.

PAGE 11: Lesson 1: My name and what makes me unique — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Why do you say your name in class?

2. What does unique mean?

3. What does Psalm 139:13 teach about you?

## Answers to practice

1. So that people can identify who I am.

2. One of a kind; not exactly like anyone else.

3. God formed me with care inside my mother.

## Summary
• Saying your name helps people identify you.
• You are unique because God made you one of a kind.
• Psalm 139:13 teaches that God formed you with care.

PAGE 12: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God

LESSON 2: CREATED IN THE IMAGE OF GOD
=====================================

## What you will learn
• Acknowledge God as the Creator.
• Read Genesis 1:27 about being created in the image and likeness of God.
• Appreciate himself or herself as God's special creation.

Curriculum outcomes: c) acknowledge God as the creator; d) appreciate his or her uniqueness as God’s special creation

## Introduction
Look at your hands, your eyes and the friends sitting near you. People did not make themselves. The Bible teaches that God is the Creator, and that He made people in His image.

PAGE 13: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — God is the Creator

## Notes

### God is the Creator
To acknowledge God as the Creator means to agree that He made the world and He made you. The sun, the plants, the animals and people all come from His work. You are not an accident. You are a creation of God.

PAGE 14: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Genesis 1:27

### Genesis 1:27
Genesis 1:27 says that God created human beings in His own image and likeness. He created them male and female. Image and likeness do not mean that God has a body like ours. They mean that people can know God, love, choose, speak and care for what He has made.

Because every person is made in God's image:

- You have value that does not depend on marks, clothes or height.
- Other children have the same value. You should not insult them.
- Boys and girls are both God's creation.

PAGE 15: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Appreciating God's special creation

### Appreciating God's special creation
To appreciate means to be thankful and to treat something as precious. You appreciate yourself as God's special creation when you:

- Thank God for your life, your name and your body.
- Take care of your body by washing, eating well and resting.
- Use your gifts to help your family and your class.
- Refuse to say, "I am useless," because God does not make useless people.

Singing a song about being God's child is one way to show this thanks. Drawing your face and writing "I am God's special creation" under it is another. When you meditate on Genesis 1:27, you remember that the God who made the world also made you.

PAGE 16: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Key words

## Key words
• creator — the one who makes something; God made the world and people
• image of God — people are made to reflect God by knowing Him, loving and choosing
• appreciate — to be thankful and to treat something as precious

PAGE 17: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Example 1

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A boy laughs at a classmate who is shorter than the others. How does Genesis 1:27 correct him?

Working:
1. Genesis 1:27 says God created people in His image.
2. Height does not decide a person's value.
3. Both boys are God's special creation and should respect each other.

Answer: He should stop laughing. God made both of them in His image, so each one is special.

PAGE 18: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Read Genesis 1:27 and sing

## Activity: Read Genesis 1:27 and sing
You will need: Bible, Exercise book, Coloured pencils

1. Read Genesis 1:27 aloud in turns.

2. In pairs, say what it means to be created in the image and likeness of God.

3. Each learner draws his or her face and writes one sentence thanking God the Creator.

4. Sing a song related to your uniqueness as God's special creation.

PAGE 19: Lesson 2: Created in the image of God — Answers to practice

## Practice

1. Who is the Creator of human beings?

2. What does Genesis 1:27 say about how God created people?

3. Give one way you can appreciate yourself as God's special creation.

## Answers to practice

1. God.

2. God created them in His own image and likeness, male and female.

3. Any one: thank God for my life; take care of my body; use my gifts to help others; refuse to call myself useless.

## Summary
• God is the Creator of the world and of people.
• Genesis 1:27 says people are created in God's image and likeness.
• You show appreciation by thanking God and respecting yourself and others.

PAGE 20: Revision quiz

REVISION QUIZ
=============

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. What does self-awareness mean?
   A. Knowing who you are
   B. Forgetting your name
   C. Copying another person
   D. Hiding from the class

2. Why do learners say their names?
   A. To show off
   B. For identification
   C. To win a prize
   D. To change who they are

3. What does unique mean?

4. Which verse says that God formed you inside your mother?
   A. Genesis 1:27
   B. Psalm 139:13
   C. Ephesians 6:1
   D. Luke 1:37

5. "Fearfully and wonderfully made" means that God made you:
   A. by mistake
   B. with great care, in an amazing way
   C. to look like everyone else
   D. only if you score high marks

6. Who is the Creator?
   A. The class teacher
   B. God
   C. Parents only
   D. The oldest person in the family

7. Genesis 1:27 teaches that people are created in the ______ of God.
   A. shadow
   B. image and likeness
   C. house
   D. country

8. Why should you not laugh at a classmate who looks different from you?

9. Which action shows that you appreciate yourself as God's creation?
   A. Saying you are useless
   B. Thanking God and taking care of your body
   C. Copying someone else's face
   D. Refusing to say your name

10. A learner wishes she looked exactly like her friend. What should she remember?

PAGE 21: Quiz answers

ANSWERS
=======

1. A. Knowing who you are
   Self-awareness is knowing who you are, beginning with your name.

2. B. For identification
   Saying your name helps people identify you.

3. One of a kind.
   A unique person is not exactly like anyone else.

4. B. Psalm 139:13
   Psalm 139:13 teaches that God formed each person with care before birth.

5. B. with great care, in an amazing way
   The words mean God made you carefully and wonderfully.

6. B. God
   Christians acknowledge God as the Creator of the world and of people.

7. B. image and likeness
   The verse says God created human beings in His image and likeness, male and female.

8. Because every person is God's special creation, made in His image.
   Respect follows from knowing that God made each person unique.

9. B. Thanking God and taking care of your body
   Appreciation is shown by thanks and by caring for the life God gave you.

10. God made her unique and wonderfully, so she does not need to copy her friend.
   Psalm 139 and Genesis 1:27 teach that each person is God's special work.

questions.explanation: Psalm 139 and Genesis 1:27 teach that each person is God's special work.
